purpose: Integrates WP 6.8's Speculative Loading API (speculation rules) to enable browser-level prefetching/prerendering, with a UI toggle in Preload Settings and automatic enhancement when static cache is active.
riskRationale: Two critical bugs exist: (1) user speculation mode/eagerness settings are silently ignored when static cache is disabled, and (2) a PHP Warning is emitted for logged-in users due to a missing is_array() guard on a null config value. Both are straightforward to fix but currently cause silent misbehavior and error-log pollution.

text: The PR correctly follows the described plan — gating on function_exists(), excluding sensitive paths, and adding the UI toggle. The PHP backend has two critical bugs that must be fixed before merge: the speculation mode/eagerness settings are not applied when cache is off, and a missing is_array() guard causes a PHP Warning for logged-in users. An additional important concern is that static cache auto-enables speculation with no user opt-out. The JS and tests are clean and well-structured.

reasoning: Critical bug: user speculation settings are ignored when cache is disabled. Critical PHP Warning: missing is_array($config) guard for null config (logged-in users). Both must be fixed before merge.

message: Default settings in JS correctly mirror PHP defaults with the spread-first-override pattern, keeping frontend and backend in sync.

Tests cover the three critical states: hidden by default, revealed on toggle, and payload submission. The use of expect.objectContaining() in the submit test is the right pattern for partial-object verification.
The function_exists() gate on wp_get_speculation_rules_configuration provides clean backward compatibility for sites not yet on WP 6.8.

The wp_speculation_rules_configuration filter callback only applies mode/eagerness when $cache_enabled is true, but the filter is registered whenever $enable_speculation is true without $cache_enabled. This means a user who explicitly enables speculation rules (toggle ON) but has static cache OFF will see the UI reflect their mode/eagerness choices, but the filter never applies them — speculation runs with core defaults (prefetch + conservative) instead of the user's selection.
suggestion: Remove the inner if ( $cache_enabled ) guard so the mode/eagerness settings are always applied when the filter is active. The outer if ( $cache_enabled || $enable_speculation ) already ensures the filter is only registered when speculation should be active.

message: Missing is_array( $config ) check. WordPress 6.8 passes null for the $config parameter when a user is logged in or when pretty permalinks are disabled. Setting $config['mode'] and $config['eagerness'] directly on null emits a PHP 8.x Warning (Cannot use a scalar value as an array). While the assignments silently fail on null (speculation stays disabled for logged-in users), the PHP Warning pollutes error logs.
suggestion: Wrap the configuration assignments in an if ( is_array( $config ) ) check, matching the pattern used in WordPress core documentation examples.

message: When static cache is enabled ($cache_enabled), speculation rules are always activated with defaults (prerender + moderate) regardless of the user's enableSpeculationRules toggle. A user who wants static cache but does NOT want speculation (e.g., due to analytics double-counting or bandwidth concerns) currently has no way to opt out without disabling the cache.
suggestion: Gate the automatic cache-triggered speculation behind a more explicit condition. Either respect enableSpeculationRules (if false, skip speculation even when cache is on) or add a separate sub-setting for cache-auto-speculation.
